item.title: 12) The quantum harmonic oscillator and a brief 3D glimpse
item.description: The quantum harmonic oscillator and a brief 3D glimpse The particle in a box, the finite well, and tunneling barriers all showed the same basic rule: the potential energy function U(x) shapes the allowed wave functions.

item.title: 10) The time-independent Schrödinger equation and the particle in a box
item.description: The time-independent Schrödinger equation and the particle in a box The previous subsection gave the wave function a physical interpretation.

item.title: 9) Interpreting wave functions and wave packets
item.description: Interpreting wave functions and wave packets The free-particle Schrödinger equation gave us a rule for how a matter wave evolves: i\hbar\frac{\partial \Psi}{\partial t} = -\frac{\hbar^2}{2m} \frac{\partial^2\Psi}{\partial x^2}.

item.title: 8) From matter waves to the free-particle Schrödinger equation
item.description: From matter waves to the free-particle Schrödinger equation The De Broglie relation gave matter a wavelength: \lambda=\frac{h}{p}.

item.title: 7) Lasers and blackbody radiation as quantization applications
item.description: Lasers and blackbody radiation as quantization applications The Bohr model showed that atoms do not exchange arbitrary amounts of energy with light.
